label: CRS304-4XG-IN
description: MikroTik CRS304-4XG-IN (CRS304-4XG-IN) — 1x 1G RJ45, 4x 10G RJ45. Powered by two DC jacks, a 2-pin terminal, or 802.3af/at PoE-in on the eth5 MGMT/BOOT port (36-57 V). ARM 64bit 2-core 98DX2528.
notes: Vendor rows read 2026-11-28 from https://mikrotik.com/product/crs304_4xg_in: **Number of DC inputs 4 (DC jack, PoE-IN, 2-pin terminal)**, **PoE in 802.3af/at**, **DC jack input Voltage 12-57 V / 12-57 V**, **2-pin terminal input Voltage 12-57 V**, **Max power consumption 21 W**, **Max power consumption without attachments 15 W**. https://manual.mikrotik.com/hardware/crs304-4xg-in/ names the socket and the voltage window: "The device can be powered through two DC power jacks ... a 2-pin terminal, or the MGMT/BOOT Ethernet PoE-in port ... MGMT/BOOT Ethernet PoE-in port accepts passive or 802.3af/at Power over Ethernet in the range of DC 36-57 V" and "The power consumption of this device is 21 W at maximum load and 15 W at minimum". The MGMT/BOOT port is the fifth interface: the manual's "One Gigabit Ethernet port, suggested to be used for management" sits beside "Four 1G/2.5G/5G/10G Ethernet ports", and RouterOS names it ether5 (bridge-port listings in MikroTik's own forum threads put ether1-ether4 on the 10G block and ether5 alone on the management port). So eth5 is the inlet at the 21 W full-load ceiling; eth1-eth4 declare poeIn: false, since the four 10G sockets carry data only and the board sources no PoE. The four silent 10G sockets had been inheriting the 12.95 W guess from the poe-pd capability (51.8 W from a 21 W switch); at 802.3af the 36-57 V window and 12.95 W PD allowance are both short of that ceiling, which is the 802.3at half of the vendor's "802.3af/at".
